search box works well, but any post with a date prior to 2025 should be considered archived information . the college admission process changes every year! if you are a reporter, please contact the office of university communications for current, official information. welcome to the blog and thanks for reading! wednesday, september 02, 2026 customizing the common app essay for uva it's natural to look for advice from trusted voices when you're doing something important for the first time. i think it's wonderful that there are so many people trying to help students through the college application process. that being said, i continue to see college admission influencers on social media suggest that students should customize their common application essay for every school on their list. i made a video about this back in june , but it bears repeating here on the blog: your common app essay should address the common app prompts. more recently, i've seen people suggest that for uva, the common app essay must be about an intended major and/or address "why uva." with two small exceptions*, we don't admit to majors at uva and we've never had a "why uva" essay in the 20 years i've been here. we don't expect you to have a major finalized yet and we have years of surveys and anecdotes that tell us why people find uva appealing. the essay is your opportunity to share something meaningful about yourself. a strong essay gives readers insight into your experiences, perspective, and interests. it doesn't have to be about a specific one college. if you're happy with your common app essay and it shares something interesting about you that doesn't come through in the other parts of the application, there's no need to rewrite it just to mention uva or one of our academic programs. focus on telling your story well. authentic voice, style, and tone is far more important than trying to work a college's name into an essay where it doesn't naturally belong. as always, remember that the application is made up of many important parts. the essay is one piece of the puzzle. *the common app and our application instructions explain that we admit students to the college of arts & sciences (undeclared), school of engineering (undeclared), school of architecture (undeclared), school of nursing, and the kinesiology program. posted by dean j at labels: common app , essays thursday, july 30, 2026 advice for filling out the common app activity section for uva (all in one place) i've written about the common app activity section more times than i can count over the years, and i keep noticing the same handful of questions coming up again and again on reddit, in info sessions, in the dms on social media, and during travel season. if you click on the "activities" tab on this blog to see all the things i've written over the years, you'll realize that the concerns students have about this section haven't changed all that much over the years and neither has my advice (with one exception, addressed below). i thought it was time to pull all of that together into one post. consider this the "greatest hits" of my activity section advice. activities don't have to align with a possible major almost all of the students at uva arrive undeclared (exceptions are those studying nursing or kinesiology). even those who have ideas about what they want to study often change their minds once they get here and start taking classes. after all, you haven't even had access to the variety of disciplines colleges offer when you're in high school. activities should be interesting and rewarding to you . explore your possible academic interests through activities if you want to, but it isn't a requirement, and it never has been. the orchestra will assemble at larger schools back in the olden days (the 1990s) when i was disappointed by one of my college decisions, a family member giving me a spiel about how someone's daughter got into a certain really selective college because they played the french horn. it did not make me feel better. it made the admission process feel totally capricious. looking back, i now know that person would have had to have an all-around awesome application to get into that school. they didn't get picked because of the french horn. oh my gosh, was that horrible "pep talk" part of my origin story? maybe. anyway... with 18,000 students at uva and 4,000 new students joining us every year, we don't need to manufacture variety when it comes to the interests and talents present here. there will be dancers. there will be robotics kids and theater kids and kids building a sneaker flipping drop-shipping tiktok clipping side hustle. nobody on our staff is sitting there thinking "we're short on debaters this cycle." whatever you're involved in, there's room for it. that also means we don't rank activities against each other. uva has 978 student organizations on the books , and whether you're the president of a huge club at your school or in solo pursuit of something delightfully niche, we're glad you found something that mattered to you . you don't need a spike and the class will be well-rounded if you're consuming college admission content on instagram, reddit, or tiktok, you've probably run into the idea of the "spike." this is the theory that your activities (sometimes your whole application) should be packaged around an intended major. this isn't a new concept, it's just gotten a new name. when i was applying to college, this was called being a "specialist" (sometimes referred to as "pointy.") and it was the only other option if you weren't well-rounded. this is where the size of our school and each class comes into play again. admission officers know that a class of 4,000 will be well-rounded due to its size. we don't have a checklist for the kinds of activities every student should have on their activity list nor do we expect your activities to broadcast a future major. while there are certain activities that attract certain kinds of students ( *waves at the first and ootm participants* ), there is no requirement for this. they don't have to relate to each other, and they definitely don't have to relate to your academic interests. activities should be things you find interesting, rewarding, or just plain fun. by the way, we do care about well-roundedness in your academic foundation. high school is the time to build a nice foundation across many disciplines. college is where you get to specialize...after some more foundation work. a few more things worth knowing you don't have to fill the whole activity chart. filling out all ten spaces isn't the norm. you don't need to show years of unbroken commitment. it's natural for activities to change as you grow and develop! in addition, if taking on more rigorous courses in junior and senior year required a shift in time commitments, that's a completely reasonable trade-off. you'll probably have to do that in college, too. descriptions don't need to be masterpieces . you don't have to explain what deca is, just give detail about your personal involvement. the activity section helps us get a sense of how you spend your time and energy outside the classroom. it's not there so we can check boxes, fill quotas, or match you to a major. spend your high school years on the things that actually interest you, and the rest tends to take care of itself. what questions do you still have about how activities factor into the uva review process? posted by dean j at labels: student activities email momentarily. thank you for your continued interest in the university of virginia. we are grateful that you chose to remain on the waiting list – we know that waiting is never easy. after considering the size of the first-year class and the total number of offers extended, we’ve determined that we are unable to make additional offers of admission. we will close the waiting list this future. you have demonstrated that you are more than capable of thriving at uva and contributing to the education and experience of your classmates. if your heart is truly set on attending uva, we’re here to help. many waitlisted first-year students earn admission after one or two years elsewhere, provided they let us help them with planning. if you would like to talk to an admission counselor about transfer admission, we would welcome the chance to answer your questions. we appreciate your interest in the university of virginia and wish you the best as you begin your college career. sincerely, greg w. roberts associate vice provost of enrollment and admission i hope you can look at your chosen school with excitement and have plans for a wonderful summer. best wish as you prepare until aid is offered, so this could take time. thank you for your continued interest in uva! as always, i'll be going live on thursday to answer questions via instagram and i welcome your questions in the comments. posted by dean j at labels: waiting list , waitlist wednesday, april 29, 2026 "official" accounts/groups (and finding roommates) on instagram, facebook, and groupme a few years after social media opened up to more than just college students, third parties started trying to capitalize on students' and parents' desire to connect with others joining a college's community. colleges created "official" class groups, but so did companies targeting college-bound students and parents with products and services. in recent years, this has moved to instagram, groupme, and probably some other channels, too. it's hard to know who is behind the class accounts/groups, but we know it's not us. some of them are even charging students $10 to post their pictures, claiming to help with roommate searches. so here's the deal... 1. uva did not create any of the class accounts on social media . verify any information shared with official sources. call us! we're open during business hours and are happy to help. 2. uva housing has a secure, private roommate search feature in their system. you can answer some questions to build your profile and then search for people based on how they've answered questions. the class isn't final yet (the deadline to reply to an offer is midnight on friday night), so there are many potential roommates still to join you! 3. be careful about sending your image and personal information online. when you send your image and biographical information to a third party you no longer have control of it. last year, some group started selling tickets to a "welcome week" party on instagram. the party didn't exist. the website for the party was registered in iceland and i'm sure they were selling these tickets to students at lots of colleges. there are two facebook groups for parents that i know for certain got started by uva parents. one is called uva parent network (12,000 members) and the other is called uva parent discussion group (5,900 members). i am not in these groups and can't speak to the conversations there. the new "parents and families" facebook groups were created by people who have hundreds of similar accounts for colleges around the country. they might be tied to a tutoring company, but i'm not certain. posted by dean j at thursday, march 19, 2026 echols, rodman, and college science scholars, round 2 the forge new friendships, acclimate to college life and begin developing the necessary skills to flourish at w&l. “the class of 2030 includes students from 403 different secondary schools — including charter, public, parochial, independent, united world colleges and home school — who demonstrate a commitment to leadership and community engagement, and whose curiosity and ambition stood out among the 8,904 applications we received this year,” said vice president for admissions and financial aid sally stone richmond. twenty-two percent of the class are domestic students of color, 16% are the first generation in their family to attend college, and 10% are children of w&l alumni. this slideshow requires javascript. the class represents a pool of well-rounded and academically gifted leaders, with johnson scholars comprising 10% of the class and questbridge finalists making up another 10% of the class. w&l continues to recruit a geographically diverse class with 44 countries of origin and 38 u.s. states and territories represented. thirty-seven different languages are spoken at home among members of this class, and students hailing from rural areas within the u.s. comprise 17% of the class. “clearly, the composition in this class reflects the university’s commitment to affordability and access,” richmond said. “among those students receiving need-based aid, 36% of the class are w&l promise recipients. and that commitment persists: the promise will increase in 2027-28 to families earning up to $200,000 annually.” sixty-five percent of the class is receiving w&l grant assistance, and the average need- based grant is $72,696. in addition, 16% of this year’s class are federal pell grant recipients, reflecting the university’s commitment, as a member of the american talent initiative , to expanding access and opportunity for talented low- and moderate-income students. the university’s admissions team, through careful, whole-person consideration, recruits, admits and enrolls individuals who will contribute to w&l’s vibrant community and benefit from the distinct and personalized education the university offers. “we are so grateful to the entire w&l community for supporting these students’ experiences as applicants, admits and now fully enrolled members of the undergraduate student body,” richmond said. “it truly does take the entire campus community to enroll each class!” learn more about the incoming class here , and take a few moments to meet some of the members of the class of 2030 in the video below. diverse interests members of the class of 2030 include published authors, designers, youth ambassadors, founders, filmmakers, first responders, musicians, advocates, cartographers, translators, museum interpreters and state champions. they also include a bulldozer driver for hurricane cleanup, a christmas tree farmer, a voice actor, a goat herder, a cello performer, a dock hand, an auto mechanic, a haunted house actor, an ocean rescue lifeguard, a pilot and an adaptive ice-skating instructor, and they have interned for embassies, medical clinics, historical associations, international sports teams, nonprofits and more. related (photo by timothy d. sofranko) william & mary will welcome admitted undergraduate students and their families to campus this weekend to explore all that the university has to offer. more than 1,300 admitted students plus their families are expected to participate in the annual day for admitted students on april 11. the event allows admitted students to experience life at the nationally preeminent university through a series of activities that explore william & mary’s academics, research, student life and campus living offerings. in total, william & mary made 6,001 offers of admission to undergraduate applicants this year through both its early decision and regular decision processes. those applicants were selected from a pool of 17,432 — an admission rate of 34%. as part of the overall applicant pool, the university set a record for early decision applications, receiving 1,606 for the class of 2030 — up 9% from last year. “starting off the cycle with a record number of early decision applications enabled us to build an excellent foundation to the class of 2030,” said tim wolfe, associate provost for enrollment and dean of admission. “this momentum carried over into our regular decision process. based on the academic quality, experiences and talents displayed in the applications of our admitted students, i’m confident this class will make william & mary proud and be among the best of the best in the nation.” participants in last year’s event pose for a photo in front of a wren building backdrop. (photo by timothy d. sofranko) participants in last year’s day for admitted students learn about william & mary’s academic offerings. (photo by timothy d. sofranko) meet the admitted students william & mary accepts undergraduate applications through its two-phase early decision process and its regular decision process. early decision applicants received notification of their status in december and january, and regular decision applicants learned of theirs in march. in addition to setting a new record for early decision applications, the university made a record number of early decision admission offers. including both rounds, the university made 760 offers to early decision applicants. overall, the admitted students are a bright and accomplished group. of those with a class rank, 89% are in the top 10% of their class. the sat middle-50% is 1420-1520, and the act middle-50% range is 33-35. they represent 57 different countries and 50 states plus washington, d.c., puerto rico, the u.s. virgin islands, guam and northern mariana islands. after virginia, the top 10 states represented include new york, new jersey, maryland, massachusetts, pennsylvania, california, north carolina, texas, connecticut and florida. this year, the university saw a 3% increase in the number of in-state, first-generation students offered admission. in addition, the university experienced a 5% increase in the number of admitted, in-state students who applied using an application fee waiver, which can be a leading indicator of potential pell grant eligibility. william & mary has been working in recent years to increase access for limited-income and first-generation students. in 2022, the university announced an initiative to cover tuition and fees for all in-state pell grant recipients. the next year, the university launched its commonwealth impact partnership program . those efforts continue paying off, and in fall 2024, the university reached its initial goal of having pell grant recipients make up at least 20% of its in-state students. students talk with participants in last year’s event about w&m’s many student clubs and organizations. (photo by timothy d. sofranko) a student at last year’s event holds up a bell, given to students who submitted enrollment deposits. (photo by timothy d. sofranko) a day of exploring the lineup for this year’s day for admitted students includes a student organization fair, “tribe on the track,” plus a sunken garden party, mock lectures, mini tours, department chats and other sessions focused on various aspects of the university. the day will culminate in a green & gold student social in zable stadium, with a parent & family social happening at the same time. like last year, participants in this year’s day for admitted students who have submitted an enrollment deposit will receive a miniature bell with a cypher engraved on it. “we’re so looking forward to welcoming the newly admitted students to campus,” said kate perry, associate dean of admission. “our hope is these events will give visitors a genuine sense of what it’s like to be part of this close-knit and academically driven community. “we plan to introduce students and families to the endless opportunities they’ll have at william & mary with sessions focused on our newly established academic programs, multidisciplinary research, impactful and funded internships and global experiences abroad. they’ll meet with current students to learn more about campus and residential life and hear about their involvement with everything from club gymnastics to the cheese club.” admitted students unable to attend will be able to explore william & mary through two more opportunities this month: the you belong program on april 10 and green & gold days april 6, 20 and 24. both are open to all admitted students. “we hope students and families leave with a sense of of 2030 through its early action program, the office of undergraduate admissions announced today. among all 7,140 early action applicants, 18% were deferred for reconsideration in the spring, 70% were denied admission, and 1% were withdrawn or incomplete. “the students admitted through early action impressed the admissions committee with their broad range of academic achievements, their significant contributions to countless communities, and their myriad talents,” said jeremiah quinlan, dean of undergraduate admissions and financial aid. “i was thrilled to see so many of the world’s highest-achieving students identifying yale as a top choice in their college search.” yale does not require students who are offered admission through the early action program to enroll; admitted students will have until may 1, 2026 to reply to yale’s invitation to join the class of 2030. earlier this month, yale college also admitted 118 students through the questbridge college match program. questbridge is a national nonprofit organization that connects academically accomplished students from lower-income backgrounds with selective colleges and universities. this year, questbridge matched 2,550 students at 55 partner schools . the 118 questbridge “matches” for yale set a new record — 35% higher than the previous record, in 2019 (87), with 52 more students admitted than last year (66). since yale became a questbridge partner in 2007, more than 1,500 students affiliated with the organization have enrolled in yale college. students admitted through the questbridge match program qualify for yale’s most generous financial aid award — the “zero parent share” award. in addition to covering the full cost of tuition, housing, and meals, yale will provide hospitalization insurance coverage and a $2,000 start-up grant in each student’s first year. yale college meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for all students without requiring students or their families to take out loans. among the 1,640 students in the current first-year class , 54% are receiving a yale need-based financial award with an average scholarship of $75,854. the admissions office has invited all newly admitted students to visit campus in april 2026 for bulldog days, a three-day immersive experience of life at yale, or for bulldog saturday, a one-day program offering campus tours, panels, academic forums, and student performances. the admissions office will also host virtual events, online communities, and local in-person events with yale alumni to help admitted students connect with each other and with the yale community prior to bulldog days. admitted students from lower-income families receive financial support to visit campus during bulldog days so that they can experience campus life before replying to their offers of admission. last year the admissions office’s yale travel program offered travel grants to more than 600 admitted students. in january, the admissions office will turn its attention to the much larger group of applicants who opt to apply through the regular decision program. those students will receive their admissions decisions on march 26. media
